title: Review whether learning justified retaining or changing the affected mechanisms

scenarios: Bootstrap review challenges seven skills and centralized state
Correction is preserved as decision rationale rather than obsolete implementation
Evidence or memory proposes but does not silently redefine intent
Previously approved Golden Path architecture is reconsidered when its justification no longer holds
Retaining sufficient architecture without manufacturing implementation changes
Current runtime bindings are distinguished from portable engineering doctrine
spec.passCriteria: Reviewer traces observation, root cause, current requirement and justified choice to add, change, retain, consolidate, replace or remove a mechanism. Consequential changes have an appropriate human decision before implementation, preserve required behavior and controls, and retain explainable historical rationale. Retention needs reasoning, not a forced diff. Actual proof, approval scope and remaining uncertainty are explicit; structural validity alone is insufficient.
spec.procedure: Review the relevant decisions, Git/review history and any implementation diff with actual check output. Use the learning and architecture references to compare the strongest simpler option, including retention or removal. Check that current bindings resolve after removal and that prior reasoning is recoverable without retaining obsolete code or adding a ledger. Treat runtime-specific discovery checks as bootstrap bindings, not universal doctrine. Record an actual human review result as evidence only after review; these scenarios are defined, not claimed executed.
